flawed_step: The step that would show every vertex of T has an incoming arc and an outgoing arc cannot be justified. A Hamiltonian cycle needs every vertex to have in-degree and out-degree at least 1, but a tournament can have a source, a vertex whose arcs all point outward. By Camion's theorem, a tournament has a Hamiltonian cycle only when it is strongly connected, and not every tournament on 4 vertices is.
counterexample: The transitive tournament on vertices {1,2,3,4} with arc i→j whenever i<j. Vertex 1 has in-degree 0, so no directed cycle passes through it. In fact this tournament is acyclic.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. To prove it, you would need every vertex to lie on a directed cycle, which forces in-degree at least 1 at every vertex. That fails for any tournament with a source. The transitive 4-vertex tournament (i→j for i<j) has no directed cycles at all, so it has no Hamiltonian cycle. Only strongly connected tournaments are Hamiltonian (Camion's theorem).
